div.head: II Em 4
div.ab: Eac ic cyðe, þæt ic nelle socne habban to minum hirede, ær he hæbbe godcunde bote underfangen ⁊ wið þa mægðer gebet on bote befangen ⁊ to ælcum rihte gebogen, swa biscop him tæce, ðe hit on his scyre sy.

Eac ic cyðe, þæt ic nelle socne habban to minum hirede, ær he hæbbe godcunde bote underfangan ⁊ wið ða mægðe gebet on bote befangen ⁊ to ælcum rihte gebogen, swa biscop him tæce, ðe hit on his scyre sy.

Amplius indico, quod eum qui sanguinem fundet humanum nolo socnam habere in familiam meam, antequam diuinam emendationem susceperit et ad omne rectum inclinetur, sicut episcopus docebit, in cuius scira fuerit.

[Be blodgeote.] Eac ic cyðe, þæt ic nelle socne habban [þone ðe mannes blod geote] to minum hirede, ær he hæbbe g[od]cunde bote underfangen ⁊ wið ða mægðe gebet—on bote befangen— ⁊ to ælcum rihte gebogen, swa biscop him tæce ðe hit on his scyre sy.

(Von Blutvergiessen. Ld). Ferner thue ich kund, dass ich (den, der Menschenblut vergiesst lq) nicht zu meinem Hofe Zuflucht finden [lassen] will, bevor er kirchlicher Busse sich unterzogen und gegenüber der Sippe [des Erschlagenen die von ihr] geforderte[?] Busse auf sich genommen und jeder Rechtspflicht sich unterworfen hat, wie der Bischof ihm vorschreibt, der es in jenes [Thäters] Sprengel ist.

(Of bloodshed. Ld) Further I make known that I will not [let] (him who sheds human blood, lq) find refuge at my court until he has undergone ecclesiastical penance and taken upon himself the compensation demanded[?] [by] the kindred [of the slain man] and submitted to every legal obligation, as the bishop in whose diocese that [offender] is prescribes for him.

Further, I declare that I forbid anyone [who commits homicide] to have right of access to my household, until he has undertaken to make amends as the church requires, and has made—or set about making—reparation to the kin, and has submitted to every legal penalty prescribed by the bishop in whose diocese it is.

Further, I make it known that I will allow no resort to my court before he [the slayer] has undergone ecclesiastical penance and undertaken the prescribed compensation to the kindred, and submitted to every legal obligation, as the bishop, in whose diocese it is, instructs him.

div.note: H lacks the subject; Liebermann would supply from Ld ‘þone þe mannes blod geote’ (so Quadr.). H's ‘þa mægðer’ is corrected to ‘mægðe’ from Ld (B: ‘ðam ægðe’); ‘gebet’ perhaps for ‘gebeden(e) bote’. Liebermann compares I Em 3.

sacne (‘reum’) zu emendieren, empfiehlt Steenstrup Danelag 212 unnötig.—An þone nimmt Schmid mit Unrecht Anstoss: es ist Subjekt in dem von ‘wollen’ abhängigen Accus. c. infin. (Koch-Zupitza Engl. Gram. II 112)

Steenstrup Danelag 212 recommends, unnecessarily, emending to sacne (‘reum’).—Schmid wrongly takes offence at þone: it is the subject in the acc. c. infin. dependent on ‘will’ (Koch-Zupitza Engl. Gram. II 112)

Die Zeile ⁊—befangen enthält freilich Verderbnisse und ward daher von Q als unverstanden fortgelassen, oder übersprungen, weil 2 Zeilen -fangen endeten; aber sie darf nicht mit Schmid für interpoliert gelten. Sie fehlt in I Em, nur weil dort das synodale Stück die Kirchenbusse betont

The line ⁊—befangen does admittedly contain corruptions, and was therefore omitted by Q as not understood, or skipped because 2 lines ended in -fangen; but it must not be regarded as interpolated, as Schmid holds. It is lacking in I Em only because there the synodal piece emphasizes ecclesiastical penance

Meinen Einfall gesem halt ich jetzt für verfehlt. Ich schlage nun vor, l’, was oððe zu lesen war und von Ld als -e verkannt ward, hinter gebet einzusetzen: ‘der Sippe Busse geleistet [oder] auf Busse sich eingelassen und . . .’. Ebenso Toller Suppl. 71: ‘set his hand to the work of making bot to the kin’; allein er lässt gebet stillschweigend fort. Price hält gebet, Thorpe on b. bef. für irrig in den Text geratene Randglosse; allein so gewöhnliche Wörter wie die umgebenden bedurften keiner Randglosse; auch glossierte man nicht durch Wörter vom selben Stamme wie das zu Erklärende

I now consider my conjecture gesem mistaken. I now propose inserting after gebet an l’, which was to be read as oððe and was misread by Ld as -e: ‘has made compensation to the kindred [or] has undertaken to make compensation and . . .’. Likewise Toller Suppl. 71: ‘set his hand to the work of making bot to the kin’; but he silently omits gebet. Price regards gebet, and Thorpe on b. bef., as a marginal gloss that has strayed into the text; but words as common as those surrounding them needed no marginal gloss; nor did one gloss with words of the same stem as the word being explained
Bessere Übs.: ‘in dessen Sprengel es [das Verbrechen vorgefallen] ist’
Better translation: ‘in whose diocese it [the crime has taken place]’
Nicht ‘Shire’, wie mit Q bisherige Übersetzer. Schmid 651b versteht richtig ‘Diözese’
Not ‘Shire’, as previous translators have it, following Q. Schmid 651b rightly understands ‘diocese’
The words added from Ld (cf. Q: eum qui sanguinem fundet humanum) seem to be necessary for the sense.
i.e. for refuge parallel to the sanctuary provided by the Church.

It is to be suspected that the words on bote befangen are an addition to the original text, perhaps entered above the line as an alternative to gebet. Liebermann suggests (iii. p. 127) that Ld’s gebete is due to a misreading of gebet l' (i.e. vel).
